hints.title: Streaming Multi-List Traversal
hints.text: Elements are stored across nested sub-lists that may include empty rows. How can pointers maintain state between successive item retrievals?

hints.title: Lazy Row Pointer Advancement
hints.text: Keep track of active outer row and inner column indices. Advance the outer pointer forward whenever the inner index reaches or exceeds the current row length.

hints.title: Helper Advance Blueprint
hints.text: Create a private helper advance(): while row < len(vec) and col >= len(vec[row]), increment row and reset col = 0. hasNext() calls advance() and returns row < len(vec). next() calls hasNext(), reads vec[row][col], increments col, and returns the val.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: total elements across all sub-lists
complexity.notes: Row and column pointers advance linearly without duplicating list memory.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Pre-flattening the entire structure copies all elements into a new buffer, taking O(N) space and failing for streaming input.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Constant auxiliary space lazily skips empty sub-lists upon demand.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Properly handling consecutive empty rows like [[], [1, 2], [], [], [3], []].
